_README: Durable notes surfaced in the Fix queue tab of reports/site-report.html.
The report is regenerated in full every run, so notes MUST live here — anything typed into the HTML is lost on the next run.
Keys are scraper names exactly as they appear in scrapers/scraper-registry.js, plus two special keys.
Each scraper value: { note: string, priority: 'high'|'normal'|'low', added: 'YYYY-MM-DD' }.
_global: one note shown above the Fix queue and applied to every fix.

_pending: OBJECT keyed by scraper name -> { what, expect, confirm, added }. A change already made whose effect has not been observed yet. Shown as an AWAITING badge on that scraper's Coverage row and in its Fix queue detail. Delete the key once confirmed.
A note on a scraper with no detected issues still shows up in the Fix queue, so this doubles as a to-do list.

_global.note: STOP before doing WordPress-{state} selector work. Measured 2026-08-05 with scripts/find-duplicate-library-urls.js: 355 domains are shared across two or more ACTIVE states, covering 1073 of the ~4069 configured library entries. The seed data was generated by guessing '{city}library.org' from the city name, so madisonlibrary.org is assigned to libraries in 11 states, greenvillelibrary.org in 10, franklinlibrary.org in 10. A domain can be the real site of at most one of them. Until the URLs are corrected, a scraper returning 0 events may simply be pointed at another state's library — and broadening extraction would ingest that other library's events under the wrong name and state. Fix URLs before selectors. General discipline: read SCRAPER-FIX-LOG.jsonl first, verify claims before acting, run `node -c` on every modified scraper, and append one line per logical fix to SCRAPER-FIX-LOG.jsonl. SECOND SEED-DATA DEFECT, measured 2026-08-05: the same generator also fabricated county names by appending ' County' to the city ('Arcadia County', 'Brandon County', 'Archer County' -- none are real counties). Across the 20 active WordPress-{state} library files, 2065 of 2137 county values (96.6%) fail getCountyCentroid() lookup; only 72 resolve. Worst: NY 416 bad, MA 231, PA 206, NJ 166; VT/TN/KY/MS/WV are 100% bad. Effect: the county-centroid tier of the geocoding chain is effectively dead for this entire family, so any library whose address/city geocode fails lands on the STATE centroid. This is the same class of work as the URL remediation and needs a real city-to-county data source -- do not guess counties one at a time. ADDED 2026-08-07: two cross-cutting items intentionally NOT queued as ordinary daily fix work, because CLAUDE.md's Scraper Naming rules explicitly say not to open a mass renaming campaign from a daily diagnosis, and because the verification backlog below is too large for incidental fixing: (1) SCRAPER-NAME CONFORMANCE — 315 of 464 distinct scraper_name values (68%) still drift from the two legal forms in CLAUDE.md, essentially flat versus the prior baseline (not a regression, just proportional growth). Two scrapers are COLLAPSED (MacaroniKid-MD: 20 sites under 1 name; MacaroniKid-DE: 2 sites under 1 name) and need per-site slugs first since collapsing violates the no-aggregation rule. A full remediation is a deliberate, scoped migration project the project owner should explicitly greenlight (likely phased by scraper family, largest offenders first), not something to execute piecemeal from this file. (2) VERIFICATION BACKLOG — 254 pre-existing UNVERIFIABLE zero-event library rows from prior audit cycles (bot-blocks, JS-only widgets, timeouts) have never been re-checked; a dedicated task chip was spawned for this (title: 'Re-verify 254 UNVERIFIABLE zero-event library sites') rather than attempting it inside a daily run — pick it up as its own session when convenient, batching WebFetch checks across parallel subagents per the Step 3d pattern.

local-scraper-runner.js.note: Not a registry scraper — a shared-infra note so this stays visible in the Fix queue. Fixed 2026-08-06: MacaroniKid group runs (MacaroniKid-Group1/2/3, spawned by runMacaroniGroup() since the 2026-08-04 dead-stub fix) were rendering as 'FAILED — unknown error' in scraper-summary.log even when the child process exited 0 and saved real events. formatSummaryRow() branches on r.success, but the success-path return value had no success flag, so !r.success was always true. Fixed by adding success: true/false to all three return branches in runMacaroniGroup(). CONFIRM on the next MacaroniKid group run (any of Group 1/2/3): the per-scraper table in scrapers/logs/scraper-summary.log should show a normal zero-stats success row for e.g. MacaroniKid-Group2, not a FAILED line, whenever the child process actually exits 0. Delete this note once a post-fix group run has been observed.

All 79 colliding entries were mapped to their real parent system via the State Library of NC directory; see reports/nc-url-audit.md. NOTE: an earlier recommendation in that file to delete 18 entries as 'already covered elsewhere' was REVERSED the same day — it used circular evidence and mistook scrape-time FOUND counts for database coverage. wordpress-NC is in fact the second-largest library event producer in NC with 275 rows. Establish 'covered elsewhere' only with scripts/verify-coverage.js, never by matching venue names. QUEUE UPDATE 2026-08-06: 30 of 89 entries are now verified. The remaining 59 are 50 still-colliding plus 9 that were never checked because their domain does not collide (bunnlibrary.org, dobsonlibrary.org, farmvillelibrary.libguides.com, hickorylibrary.org, indiantraillibrary.org, kinglibrary.org, louisburglibrary.org, roanokerapidslibrary.org, starlibrary.org). A non-colliding domain is still a guessed domain - verify those 9 the same way. See reports/nc-url-audit.md. Alamance County Public Library removed 2026-08-07 as verified-covered by LibCal-NC (48 events live). FIX-QUEUE 2026-08-07: (1) Bath Community Library — configured eventsUrl resolves to the site's homepage, not an actual events page; find and set the real listing URL. (2) Pinebluff Public Library and Leath Memorial Library — both on srls.info, which now runs on a LibGuides platform this DOM scraper cannot read; needs either a LibGuides-aware extraction path or an ICS/API alternative, not a selector tweak.

WordPress-MD.note: MARYLAND, state after the 2026-08-06 fixes and two live verification runs. Config is 10 entries, all counties resolving. Ruth Enlow (Garrett) and Kent County were added and both work: 3 and 22 events. Four guessed /events paths were replaced with real calendar URLs found on each library's own site. Two entries were REMOVED as verified-covered-elsewhere: Queen Anne's (33 DB rows from calendar.qaclibrary.org) whose /events served a Squarespace 404, and Washington County Free (28 rows from wcfl.librarymarket.com). OUTCOME: found rose 163 to 310, but NEW only 82 to 80 and INVALID rose 6 to 135. The URL fixes surfaced an extraction bug rather than adding saved events. ST MARY'S IS THE WHOLE STORY: its corrected URL now returns 147 events, but the generic WordPress selectors grab the time field as the date ('10 a.m.', '9:30 a.m.', '2:30 p.m.Registration'), so nearly all fail date parsing. St Mary's is also configured in Communico-MD at stmalib.libnet.info/events, which is the right parser for its LibNet platform - but Communico-MD produces ZERO St Mary's rows, so it cannot simply be removed here. Fixing Communico-MD for St Mary's is the correct path; until then WordPress-MD keeps the entry and the INVALID count is a true signal, not noise. STILL ZERO: Somerset County (somelibrary.org/events.php returns nothing). NEAR ZERO: Charles County 1, Dorchester 1 - both are real pages whose events are JS-rendered or on a separate platform (Charles is Communico at ccplonline.libnet.info). RESOLVED 2026-08-07: St. Mary's and Charles County were removed from this scraper because Communico-MD demonstrably covers both - verified by watching its run produce 5 rows for each. INVALID fell from 135 to 5 and saved events held at 79 (was 80), confirming the 147 St. Mary's events had never been saving. Remaining: Somerset County still returns 0. SOMERSET DIAGNOSED 2026-08-07 (not fixable by this scraper): somelibrary.org/events.php has a body of only 493 characters and no dates - all its events live in TWO EMBEDDED GOOGLE CALENDAR IFRAMES covering five calendar IDs. No DOM scraper can reach cross-origin iframe content, so this entry will return 0 forever. The events ARE reachable: each calendar exposes a public ICS feed at https://calendar.google.com/calendar/ical/<ID>%40group.calendar.google.com/public/basic.ics, verified 2026-08-07 returning HTTP 200 with 468KB and 152KB of real VEVENT data. The five IDs are somelibrary.org_jh8uo8466kov1vth331eje1t7s, _91sbe6asf4phciq8lcn2rlaf1k, _gcd8aeg949e1f9aobi8j418ab8, _qkhpuchqt21ec8sic3fu9chveo and _9871gfpt9lofa0cotrpciutcsg. node-ical is already a dependency (scraper-pratt-library-MD.js uses it). Implementing this needs an ICS extraction path and a filter for upcoming events, since the feeds carry history back to 2022 - it is a new capability, not a URL fix, so it was recorded rather than bolted onto a DOM scraper. SOMERSET RESOLVED 2026-08-07: removed from this scraper and now covered by the new GoogleCalendar-MD, which reads the five ICS feeds behind its Google Calendar iframes - 126 events saved, 0 invalid. WordPress-MD is now 7 entries and every Maryland library is either producing events, covered by its correct platform scraper, or has a recorded verified reason.

BarnesNoble-Eastern.note: RESOLVED 2026-08-05 by a shared fix, not a per-store one: 15 B&N stores were flagged at or above 70 percent All Ages because detectAgeRange() had no concept of 'storytime' - the most common children's program name at bookstores and libraries - so every bare 'Weekly Storytime' / 'Saturday Storytime' defaulted to All Ages. A storytime rule (Preschool 3-5) plus a tots/tykes rule (1-3) were added to supabase-adapter.js, placed AFTER every specific keyword so qualified titles like 'Toddler Storytime' still win on their own rule. Backfill reclassified 2677 rows platform-wide. Re-run to confirm these stores' All-Ages share drops.

Communico-MD.note: CORRECTION 2026-08-07: an earlier note here claimed Communico-MD produced zero rows. That was wrong - it was read from stale data before the scraper had been run. A live run on 2026-08-07 produced 86 found / 72 new, with 52 rows landing across all seven MD libraries: Montgomery County 16, Baltimore County 15, Harford 8, St. Mary's 5, Charles County 5, Calvert 2, Anne Arundel 1. This scraper is healthy. Its rows previously carried no source_url, only a per-event url, which is why verify-coverage.js could only answer INCONCLUSIVE for every library it owns; sourceUrl: library.url has now been added to both of its metadata blocks.

GoogleCalendar-MD.note: Built 2026-08-07 for libraries that publish only through an embedded Google Calendar iframe, where the host page carries no event markup at all and every DOM scraper returns 0 by construction. Reads the public ICS feed behind each iframe with node-ical, expands RRULE recurrences (library storytimes are almost all recurring, so this is the difference between one row and a term's worth), honours EXDATE, skips STATUS:CANCELLED, and keeps a 90-day forward window. First live run: 169 found, 126 saved, 0 invalid dates, 0 junk titles, 0 past events, with age detection splitting 87 All Ages / 21 Babies / 13 Kids / 5 Teens. Currently one library, Somerset County Library (5 calendar IDs). To add another site: open its events page, read the iframe src, and collect every src= parameter.
